diagnostic_evidence.quote:
There exists a constant $\tau_{\max}>0$ that depends on the initial function $\phi^0$ such that for any $\tau_n\in (0,\tau_{\max})$, the iterations $\{\phi^n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$
	generated by the P-RG have the following properties:

issues.failure_explanation: Part (i), summed over n, only yields $\sum_n C_{\tau_n}\|d_n\|^2_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi^n}}\le E(\phi^0)-E_g<\infty$ with $C_{\tau_n}\ge\tau_n-\tau_n^2/\tau_{\max}$. Under the stated hypothesis that $\tau_n\in(0,\tau_{\max})$ is arbitrary, $C_{\tau_n}$ can tend to 0 (e.g. $\tau_n\to0$ or $\tau_n\to\tau_{\max}$), so the summability does not imply $\|d_n\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi^n}}=\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}}E^n\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi^n}}\to0$. The inference "$\lim_n\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}}E^n\|=0$" is therefore unjustified, and with it the criticality $\mathcal{H}_{\phi_g}\phi_g=\lambda_g\mathcal{I}\phi_g$ of the limit. The failure is genuine: for summable steps (e.g. $\tau_n=\epsilon 2^{-n}$) the iterates move a finite total $H^1$ distance and can converge strongly to a non-critical point, so part (ii) is false as stated.

failure_location.quote:
Combined with {\bf Theorem \ref{Global-Convergence}}-$(i)$, we get
	\[
	\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}} E^n\right\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi^n}}=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\left\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}} E(\phi_g)\right\|_{H^1}=0.
	\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the admissible step sizes so that $C_{\tau_n}$ stays uniformly positive, e.g. require $\tau_n\in[\underline{\tau},\overline{\tau}]\subset(0,\tau_{\max})$ for all n (or $\liminf\tau_n>0$ and $\limsup\tau_n<\tau_{\max}$); the proof of (ii) then goes through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.1(ii) (existence of an $H^1$-convergent subsequence whose limit satisfies the first-order necessary condition $\mathcal{H}_{\phi_g}\phi_g=\lambda_g\mathcal{I}\phi_g$) is unproved and can fail for step sequences allowed by the statement. The sufficient-descent statement (i) is unaffected, as are the local results, which use fixed step sizes in a restricted range.
issues.title: Global convergence (Thm. 4.1(ii)) as stated allows degenerate step sizes, under which the Riemannian gradient need not tend to zero and the limit need not be critical
issues.why_classification: Adding this standard step-size non-degeneracy condition is a short, local fix: the sufficient-descent estimate, the method, and the advertised global-convergence scope all survive unchanged, and no new nontrivial lemma or replacement argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let \(\mathcal{J}_{\phi_g}: H_0^1(\mathcal{D}) \to N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}\) denote the $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}$-orthogonal projection from $H^1_0(\mathcal{D})$ onto $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$.

These convergence results rely on a special property of the ground state: the ground state of the nonlinear problem is also the unique ground state of its linearized version (cf. \cite{2010Numerical}), which cannot apply to the rotating cases ($\Omega>0$).

issues.failure_explanation: For $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}=E''(\phi_g)-(\lambda_g-\sigma_0)\mathcal{I}$, the $\sigma_0$-shift only yields $\langle\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}v,v\rangle=\langle(E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I})v,v\rangle+\sigma_0\|v\|_{L^2}^2\ge\sigma_0\|v\|_{L^2}^2$ on $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ (via the second-order necessary condition). On $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})=T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}\oplus\mathrm{span}\{\phi_g\}$ there is a nonzero coupling $2(f'(\rho_{\phi_g})|\phi_g|^2\phi_g,v)_{L^2}$ between $\phi_g$ and $v\in N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ (since $E''(\phi_g)\phi_g=\lambda_g\phi_g+2f'(\rho_{\phi_g})|\phi_g|^2\phi_g$), so positivity/coercivity on the whole space requires an additional scalar Schur-type condition $\sigma_0+2\int_{\mathcal{D}}f'(\rho_{\phi_g})|\phi_g|^4\rd\bm{x}-4\langle h,(\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}|_{N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}})^{-1}h\rangle>0$ (h the Riesz representative of that coupling on $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$). This condition is never stated or verified, it is not implied by (A1)-(A6) plus the Morse-Bott property, and for small $\sigma_0$ it can fail (the paper itself notes that in the rotating case the ground state is not the ground state of the linearized operator, so $E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I}$ need not be nonnegative off $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$). Yet full-space positivity is required for the inner product $(\cdot,\cdot)_{\mathcal{P}_\phi}$ and its norms, for the inverse $\mathcal{P}_\phi^{-1}$ and the projection formula \eqref{Proj-P}, for the $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}$-orthogonal projection $\mathcal{J}_{\phi_g}$ used in Lemmas \ref{F-diff} and \ref{G-spectrum}, and for the completing-the-square supremum over $v\in H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$ in the Polyak-Łojasiewicz proof (Lemma \ref{Polyak-Loj}), invoked through Theorem \ref{Local-Convergence}.

failure_location.quote: the sequence $\{\phi^n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ generated by the P-RG with the optimal local preconditioner \eqref{Varep-P} yields another locally linear convergence rate

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit hypothesis that $\mathcal{P}_\phi$ in \eqref{Varep-P} is coercive on $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$ for $\phi$ near $\phi_g$ (equivalently the scalar Schur positivity condition at $\phi_g$, which persists nearby by continuity of $E''$ and $\widetilde\lambda_\phi$), and identify regimes where it holds, e.g. $\Omega=0$, $f(s)=\eta s$, $\eta\ge0$, where ground-state positivity gives $E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I}\ge0$ on all of $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$ so that any $\sigma_0>0$ works.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem \ref{Var-P-convergence} (the paper's optimal-rate result) and the very well-definedness of the P-RG iteration with preconditioner \eqref{Varep-P} rest on this unverified algebraic condition. If it fails, $(\cdot,\cdot)_{\mathcal{P}_\phi}$ is not an inner product, the iteration and the objects $\mathcal{J}_{\phi_g}$, $\mathcal{G}_\tau(\phi_g)$ are not well defined, and the local analysis (Lemmas \ref{F-diff}, \ref{G-spectrum}, the PL inequality via Theorem \ref{Local-Convergence}) does not apply; the advertised 'optimal preconditioner' and the abstract/conclusion claims of achieving the optimal rate $(L-\mu)/(L+\mu)+\varepsilon$ become conditional on an unstated hypothesis.
issues.title: The 'optimal local preconditioner' (4.4) is not shown to be coercive/positive definite on $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$; the $\sigma_0$-shift gives positivity only on the tangent space
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained additional hypothesis (plus standard verification in special cases); it requires no new global proof architecture and leaves the theorem and its optimal rate intact whenever the condition holds. It exceeds a routine/typo fix because the condition is nontrivial, is not implied by the standing assumptions, can fail in the rotating regime that is the paper's focus, and its possible failure undermines the construction itself, so the central optimal-rate claim survives only conditionally.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition \ref{Property-P}(i) bounds the Rayleigh quotient by $L$ only for $v\in N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$, the $L^2$-orthogonal complement of the symmetry kernel $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{S}=\mathrm{span}\{i\phi_g,i\mathcal{L}_z\phi_g\}$ inside $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ (\eqref{Orth-Complement}). The vector $\mathrm{Proj}^{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}_{\phi_g}d_n$ to which the bound is applied lies in $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ and, for a general preconditioner satisfying (A6), retains an $O(\|d_n\|)$ component along $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{S}$. For $v=v_N+v_S$ with $v_N\in N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ and $v_S\in T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{S}$ one has $\langle(E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I})v,v\rangle=\langle(E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I})v_N,v_N\rangle\le L\|v_N\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}^2$ (the kernel component drops out), but $\|v_N\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}^2$ can strictly exceed $\|v\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}^2=\|v_N+v_S\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}^2$ because $v_S$ is generally not $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}$-orthogonal to $v_N$: e.g. on $\mathbb{R}^2=\mathbb{R}e_1\oplus\mathbb{R}e_2$ with $A=\mathrm{diag}(2,0)$ and $\mathcal{P}=I+\delta(e_1e_2^T+e_2e_1^T)$, the supremum over $N=\mathbb{R}e_1$ is 2 while the supremum over the whole plane is $2/(1-\delta^2)>2$. Hence the maximal valid constant on $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ is $\widetilde{L}:=\sup_{v\in T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}}\langle(E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I})v,v\rangle/\langle\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}v,v\rangle\ge L$ (the top eigenvalue of the corresponding Schur-complement problem), with strict inequality whenever the extremizing directions on $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ are not $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}$-orthogonal to $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{S}$ — generically the case for the standard preconditioners of Remark \ref{Proj-Sobo-Grad} (e.g. for $\mathcal{P}_\phi=a\mathcal{I}-\frac12\Delta+V(\bm{x})$, $\langle\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}(i\phi_g),v\rangle=-(if(\rho_{\phi_g})\phi_g,v)_{L^2}\neq0$ for $v\in N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$). Only for the optimal preconditioner \eqref{Varep-P} does $\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}=\sigma_0\mathcal{I}$ on $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{S}$ give $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{S}\perp_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}}N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$, hence $\widetilde L=L$. Consequently the dissipation estimate of Lemma \ref{C_t} is valid only with $\widetilde L$; for $\tau\in[2/\widetilde L,\,2/(L+\varepsilon))$ the linearized iteration has spectral radius $|1-\tau\widetilde L|>1$, so the claimed sufficient descent (and local convergence) can fail outright in the advertised step-size range.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $L$ in Lemma \ref{C_t} and Theorem \ref{Local-Convergence} by $\widetilde L:=\sup_{v\in T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}}\langle(E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal{I})v,v\rangle/\langle\mathcal{P}_{\phi_g}v,v\rangle$; the same argument then legitimately yields $E(\phi^{n+1})-E(\phi^n)\le-(\tau-\frac{\tau^2}{2}(\widetilde L+\varepsilon))\|d_n\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi^n}}^2$ for $\tau\in(0,2/(\widetilde L+\varepsilon))$ and the local rate $\sqrt{1-(\mu-\varepsilon)/(\widetilde L+\varepsilon)}$ at $\tau=1/(\widetilde L+\varepsilon)$; the numerical predictions for $\mathcal{P}_1$-$\mathcal{P}_3$ must be recomputed with $\widetilde L$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma \ref{C_t}'s constant $C_\tau=\tau-\frac{\tau^2}{2}(L+\varepsilon)$ and range $\tau\in(0,2/(L+\varepsilon))$ are invalid for general preconditioners; Theorem \ref{Local-Convergence}'s advertised rate $\sqrt{1-2C_\tau(\mu-\varepsilon)}$, its 'optimal' step $\tau=1/(L+\varepsilon)$ and rate $\sqrt{1-(\mu-\varepsilon)/(L+\varepsilon)}$ \eqref{Rate-1} are not established and can be false; the abstract/intro claims of a precise rate characterization via the condition number $\mu/L$, and the theoretical rates $\rho=\sqrt{1-\mu/L}$ used for $\mathcal{P}_1$-$\mathcal{P}_3$ in Table 2/Fig. 2, become unsupported. Theorem \ref{Var-P-convergence} is not affected by this root (for \eqref{Varep-P}, $\widetilde L=L$), and Corollary \ref{E-eq-Phi} survives since it needs only some positive dissipation constant.
issues.title: Lemma 4.4 applies the $N_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ spectral bound $L$ to general tangent vectors; the valid dissipation constant on $T_{\phi_g}\mathcal{M}$ is strictly larger, so the advertised local rate and step-size range for general preconditioners fail
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution forces the dissipation/rate constant to the strictly larger spectral quantity $\widetilde L$ over the full tangent space: the advertised rate $\sqrt{1-\mu/L}$ and optimal step $1/L$ are replaced by a worse, different guarantee, part of the advertised step-size range yields divergence rather than descent, and the paper's central claim of precisely characterizing the local rate via the condition number $\mu/L$ (including the numerical verification for the standard preconditioners) is lost. Since an important advertised rate guarantee necessarily changes and materially worsens, this is serious, even though a comparable local linear convergence theorem with $\widetilde L$ survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, in this context, we have $\mu = (\lambda_3 - \lambda_g)\big/(\lambda_3 - \lambda_g + \sigma_0)$ and $L = 1$.

Then, for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, there exist $\sigma>0$ and $\phi_g \in \mathcal{S}$ such that for all $\phi^0 \in \mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$, the sequence $\{\phi^n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ generated by the P-RG with the optimal local preconditioner \eqref{Varep-P} yields another locally linear convergence rate

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion asserts that a P-RG with superlinear local convergence rate can be achieved by reducing $\sigma_0$. What the paper proves is only: for each fixed $\sigma_0>0$ (a fixed preconditioner), the linear rate $\frac{L-\mu}{L+\mu}+\varepsilon=\frac{\sigma_0}{2(\lambda_3-\lambda_g)+\sigma_0}+\varepsilon$ holds for all $\phi^0$ in a neighborhood $\mathcal{B}_\sigma(\mathcal{S})$, with $C_\varepsilon$ and $\sigma$ depending on $\varepsilon$ and, through the preconditioner, on $\sigma_0$. Superlinearity (rate $o(q^n)$ for every $q>0$ for a given method) requires either uniformity of these constants/neighborhoods as $\sigma_0\to0$ or an analyzed adaptive schedule $\sigma_0^{(n)}\to0$; neither is established or even formulated. The formal content thus supports only 'arbitrarily fast linear rate bounds for sufficiently small fixed $\sigma_0$', not superlinear convergence.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore,  reducing $\sigma_0$ appropriately, one can achieve a P-RG with superlinear local  convergence rate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or qualify the sentence, e.g. 'reducing $\sigma_0$ improves the linear rate bound $\frac{L-\mu}{L+\mu}$, which tends to 0 as $\sigma_0\to0$'; or supply a uniformity analysis of the constants and neighborhoods as $\sigma_0\to0$, or an adaptive $\sigma_0$ schedule together with a genuine superlinearity proof.
issues.overall_effect: Only this headline-style claim in the conclusion (and, in its adaptive reading, the remark after Theorem \ref{Var-P-convergence} that one can 'gradually decrease $\sigma_0$' to obtain faster convergence); no formal result is affected.
issues.title: Conclusion claims superlinear convergence by reducing $\sigma_0$, but the theorems only give fixed-$\sigma_0$ linear rates with $\sigma_0$-dependent constants and neighborhoods
issues.why_classification: The overclaim is detachable from all formal results: deleting or qualifying it (or, at most, adding a contained uniformity discussion) preserves every substantive theorem and guarantee, so it is minor.
